answer: Staked peer review first: each reviewer puts 200 POA behind a verdict, and 5 percent of verdicts get spot-checked by a second pair drawn from a different wharf of the network. A duplicate is caught by replaying the submission against the ledger, not by matching names, so a copied text fails under a new slug. A colluding pair risks two stakes per verdict plus the spot-check odds. At the nadir of an epoch that exposure is the whole margin, and the voyage from 1 to 1,000 keys multiplies it.
